## `inline`

By declaring a function `inline`, you can direct GCC to make calls to that function faster. One way GCC can achieve this is to integrate that function's code into the code for its callers, eliminating function-call overhead.

When `inline` is used on a `static` function, GCC will not output assembler code for that function unless its address is taken or it cannot be inlined. When `inline` and `extern` are both specified, the definition is used only for inlining and is never compiled on its own.

GCC does not inline any functions when not optimizing unless the `always_inline` attribute is used.
